advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve cfg_root for the close gate consistently (e.g. reuse repo_root(repo_root)) instead of passing str(None) to gate_enabled.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/gates.py:71: `str(repo_root),`
src/rebar/_config_sources.py:35-36: `if explicit is not None: return Path(explicit).resolve()` — 'None' is not None, so Path('None').resolve() is used
src/rebar/_commands/gates.py:88: `verified = signing.verify_signature(ticket_id, kind="plan-review", repo_root=repo_root)` passes the raw (None) repo_root, not str(repo_root)
Sibling gate plan_review_precheck takes an explicit resolved `cfg_root` parameter (gates.py:113,137-138) rather than stringifying repo_root
advisory.finding: close_plan_review_gate_check passes str(repo_root) to gate_enabled; when repo_root is None this stringifies to the literal 'None', so load_config('None') resolves repo_root('None') to <cwd>/None (a nonexistent dir) and only finds the real rebar.toml via the upward parent walk. This is fragile and inconsistent with the raw repo_root=None passed to verify_signature/compute_validity in the same function.
scenarios: A CLI/library caller invokes close with repo_root=None from a nested working directory where the walk-up boundary or a stray 'None' directory changes discovery
advisory.suggested_fix: Compute a real cfg_root once (e.g. `from rebar._config_sources import repo_root as _rr; cfg_root = str(_rr(repo_root))`) and pass that to gate_enabled, matching the repo_root used for verify_signature/compute_validity.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Deduplicate the gated ticket-type set so gates and transition_close share one source of truth.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py:35: `_PLAN_REVIEW_CLOSE_TYPES = frozenset({"task", "story", "epic"})`
src/rebar/_commands/gates.py:78: `if ticket_state.get("ticket_type") not in ("task", "story", "epic"):`
src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py:554: `if not force_close and ticket_type in _PLAN_REVIEW_CLOSE_TYPES:`
advisory.finding: The set of plan-review-gated ticket types is duplicated in two places that guard the same gate: transition_close._PLAN_REVIEW_CLOSE_TYPES (frozenset) and an inline literal tuple in gates.close_plan_review_gate_check. They can drift; if one is updated to add/remove a work type the two guards disagree and the gate silently no-ops (transition_close invokes for a type gates treats as exempt) or is never invoked.
scenarios: A future ticket type (e.g. a new work type) is added to only one of the two lists
advisory.suggested_fix: Reference the same constant (e.g. import gates._PLAN_REVIEW_CLOSE_TYPES or expose one shared frozenset) in both the transition_close guard and the gates exemption check.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that `local_read_context()` resets `_LOCAL_READ_CONTEXT` to False on both normal exit and when the body raises.
evidence: src/rebar/_engine_support/reads.py:169 `def local_read_context() -> Iterator[None]:` with `token = _LOCAL_READ_CONTEXT.set(True)` / `finally: _LOCAL_READ_CONTEXT.reset(token)`
search for `local_read_context` yields only the definition (reads.py) and the single call site (gates.py:87); no test references it directly

ABSENCE: no test asserts `_LOCAL_READ_CONTEXT.get()` is False after the context manager exits, nor that the token is reset when the body raises (the gate body can raise inside the `with` at gates.py:88-95)
advisory.finding: The `local_read_context()` contextmanager's cleanup (the `finally: _LOCAL_READ_CONTEXT.reset(token)`) is untested: no test asserts the contextvar returns to False after the block exits normally or on exception. A regression that leaks the local-read suppression would globally disable freshness sync for later reads and go undetected.
scenarios: A future refactor drops or misorders the `reset(token)` and every read after a close-gate check silently skips origin/tickets reconvergence
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a unit test asserting `_LOCAL_READ_CONTEXT.get() is False` after a normal `with local_read_context(): ...` and after one whose body raises.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test where `pre_status_check` is invoked and returns normally, asserting the STATUS event is appended and the ticket reaches `closed`.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/txn.py: `if pre_status_check is not None: pre_status_check(state)` immediately before the STATUS append
tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_transition_pre_status_check.py:43-57 covers only a callback that raises; lines 65-78 cover `pre_status_check` omitted (None)
tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_plan_review_close_gate_lifecycle.py:47-66 (`test_locked_recheck_detects_change_after_precheck`) only covers the recheck FAILING/aborting
ABSENCE: no test where a non-None `pre_status_check` runs, returns normally, and the transition still reaches `closed` with the STATUS event count incremented
advisory.finding: No test exercises `pre_status_check` being invoked and returning normally (a passing recheck) while the STATUS event is still appended. The txn contract tests only cover callback-raises (abort) and callback-omitted (None); the enabled close gate is never driven end-to-end to a successful `closed` through the real transition path with the locked recheck passing.
scenarios: A regression where a passing recheck inadvertently blocks the append, or the enabled gate's recheck is wired such that a valid close never completes
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a `transition_core` test with a `pre_status_check` that records the state and returns None, asserting the ticket transitions to `closed` and the STATUS event count increases by one.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Pass the resolved repo-root string (not `str(repo_root)`) to `gate_enabled` in `close_plan_review_gate_check`, or pass `repo_root` through unchanged so `load_config(None)` resolves from cwd.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/gates.py:70-76: `if not gate_enabled(str(repo_root), "require_plan_review_for_close", ...)`

src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py:557: `check = gates.close_plan_review_gate_check(ticket_id, ticket_state, repo_root=repo_root)` where `repo_root` originates from `transition._transition_resolved(..., repo_root=None)` (src/rebar/_commands/transition.py:189 `repo_root=None` default)
src/rebar/_config_sources.py:35-36: `if explicit is not None: return Path(explicit).resolve()` — the string "None" is not None, so `Path("None").resolve()` = `<cwd>/None`, not cwd
src/rebar/config.py:387-388: cache/resolution key uses `str(root) if root is not None else None` and `os.getcwd() if root is None` — passing the string "None" defeats the None-means-cwd resolution

Contrast: the sibling claim gate passes the resolved string `repo_root_str` (src/rebar/_commands/transition.py:276 `gates.plan_review_precheck(ticket_id, repo_root_str, repo_root, ...)`), not `str(repo_root)`

The new held-out test asserts the intended (currently-unmet) behavior: tests/unit/test_plan_review_close_gate_heldout.py:104 docstring `CLI-style callers pass None; config must resolve from cwd, not "None".` with `repo_root=None` expecting `verdict == 'certified'`
dropped.finding: `close_plan_review_gate_check` stringifies `repo_root` as `gate_enabled(str(repo_root), ...)`; when the CLI close path passes `repo_root=None` (the default), this yields the literal string "None", so `config.load_config("None")` resolves the repo root to `<cwd>/None` (a nonexistent directory) instead of the real repo/cwd. The operator's `rebar.toml` enabling `require_plan_review_for_close = true` is never read, config falls to defaults (gate off), and the gate returns `verdict='disabled', ok=True` — silently fail-open, bypassing the entire close gate.
scenarios: Operator enables `verify.require_plan_review_for_close = true` in `rebar.toml` and runs `rebar transition <id> in_progress closed` via the CLI (repo_root defaults to None); the gate resolves config from `<cwd>/None`, finds no config, treats the gate as disabled, and closes the ticket with NO plan-review attestation required.
dropped.suggested_fix: Resolve the config root the same way the claim gate does — pass the already-resolved `repo_root_str` from the caller, or change the call to `gate_enabled(repo_root, ...)` (forwarding None) and let `load_config`/`_config_sources.repo_root` apply the None-means-cwd resolution, rather than `str(repo_root)`.
